summary.description: Lindane is a slightly volatile, white solid with a slight musty odour, used as an insecticide for timber. Agricultural uses have been removed in the EU.
emission_sources: Use as an insecticide for timber
Past agricultural applications (now phased out in the EU)
environmental_impact: Damages aquatic insects and fish upon release into water systems
Persists and bioaccumulates in fatty tissue of fish and the environment
Can travel long distances causing effects far from the point of release
Adverse human health effects mostly linked to occupational exposure

top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: Lindane is highly toxic to aquatic insects and fish, persists in aquatic environments, bioaccumulates, and can cause damage far from the release site.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Contamination of water bodies by lindane affects water quality and aquatic ecosystems, threatening clean water resources.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: Chronic occupational exposure to lindane has been linked to adverse human health effects, posing risks especially to agricultural workers.
